title: 2027-09-28 islandview private vpc access intake
next_steps: Send private deployment network checklist and IP worksheet
Share SOC2 + network architecture runbook link (redwood.com/security) + peering faq
Schedule 45min SE-led architecture review for Oct 4th
Spin up a short Dedicated trial tenant and share sample ingress/egress config
transcript:
Meeting header: - Date/Time: 2027-09-28 09:00 PT - Duration: ~62 minutes - Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of Cloud - IslandView), Tom Reynolds (Security Architect), Jamal Brooks (Platform) Summary: Customer evaluating Private (VPC) deployment for PII-sensitive media personalization features. Primary constraints: cross-region peering for EU customers, static egress IPs for allow-listing, and strict KMS/HSM integration. Interested in both Dedicated reservation and on-prem/private control plane options. Topics: networking topology, VPC peering vs PrivateLink, private endpoints, egress NAT/whitelisting, region gating/data residency, KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, timeline and pilot plan. 00:00 Lena Ortiz: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena from Redwood, before we start quick roll call? 00:08 Priya Nair: hey priya here, tom and jamal with me, thanks lena 00:12 Tom Reynolds: tom, security architect, i'll probably ask dumb network questions so apologies up front 00:18 Marcus Chen: marcus, se on the infra team, i'll walk through topology options 00:25 Jamal Brooks: jamal platform, curious about ips and latency numbers mostly 01:05 Lena Ortiz: great, objective for today is to understand your network posture and constraints so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private -- from what i saw in notes you want a private deployment in our vpc or self-managed? 01:16 Priya Nair: yeah our legal folks insist traffic never hit a public internet egress outside pinned regions. we have EU PII-scope, so anything serving EU customers must stay in eu-west and eu-central regions. hope that makes sense 01:31 Marcus Chen: makes sense. we have three main options: Redwood Private (customer VPC with private endpoints), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with VPC peering), or an on-prem package. For islandview sounds like private endpoints + peering fit 01:45 Tom Reynolds: on private endpoints — are those AWS privatelink endpoints or do you do skin-in-the-game with transit gw? we have a transit gateway design 01:58 Marcus Chen: we support both patterns. Common pattern is aws privatelink (interface endpoints into a Redwood-managed NLB in the redwood vpc) or direct peering to a Redwood VPC via transit gateway peering. transit is preferred for high-throughput low-latency, privatelink for strict isolation and easier allow-listing 02:18 Jamal Brooks: throughput — we have bursts during prime time, say 3k concurrent requests, avg token lengths 60 tokens. curious how batching and kv cache plays with peering 02:33 Marcus Chen: good q. our runtime uses continuous batching plus prefix/K V cache — sorry our transcripts often say K V cash — basically kv cache. with a peering connection we can keep latency to single-digit 10s of ms for short sequences assuming region-local GPU. batching is orthogonal but helps reduce cost 02:50 Tom Reynolds: ok — egress IPs, our ad partners need fixed IPs for webhooks/ingress. can you guarantee static egress ips per deployment? 03:03 Marcus Chen: yes we can provide a set of static egress IPs per deployment when you're on Dedicated or Private with NAT gateways under your control. For hosted-public we have shared egress pools which aren't suitable for allow-listing. We'll capture the exact ASN/ips in the runbook 03:20 Priya Nair: what about regional gating — can we prevent model inference from falling back to us-east in failover? 03:30 Marcus Chen: you can pin model variants and routing policies so traffic is routed by region, and we have automatic fallback options but they are configurable; you can disallow failover outside eu-west/eu-central. We'll note that we do cross-region replication for KV cache only if enabled 04:15 Lena Ortiz: quick security checklist question — SSO & audit logs, do you need SAML with IdP-initiated or do you have existing SSO? 04:26 Priya Nair: ok we use Okta, need SAML + SCIM provisioning and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also need customer-owned KMS (HSM) for key wrapping 04:38 Marcus Chen: we support SAML/Okta and SCIM; audit logs can be pushed to your S3/secure bucket or SIEM via syslog. Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated with HSM wrapping (we integrate via KMS API endpoints) 04:55 Tom Reynolds: logging — what exactly is in the audit logs? tokens? request/response? 05:03 Marcus Chen: short answer: we never log full PII payloads in production logs. We log metadata: request id, model version, token count, latency, error codes. If you need redaction we can enable redaction hooks. For full forensic, you can configure a mirror stream to your VPC for retention 05:45 Priya Nair: ok networking specifics — our infra uses Transit Gateway across accounts in prod. can redwood peer into our transit gateway or do we have to open peering at VPC-level? 05:58 Marcus Chen: we can peer into a transit gateway. Typical setup: you create a TGW attachment to a Redwood-managed VPC, or we provision a VPC in your account and attach to your TGW. Both are options; the latter gives you more control over route tables and egress NAT 06:20 Jamal Brooks: curious about IP and port requirements. our network team is picky — do you have a published list? 06:28 Lena Ortiz: yes we'll share the network checklist. it includes expected subnets, port ranges (typically 443 outbound to redwood endpoints, and some health/metrics ports for mgmt), and required peering routes. we'll send that as part of the follow-up 07:05 Tom Reynolds: latency SLA — do you have numbers for in-region private deployments vs cross-region? 07:15 Marcus Chen: in-region typically 10-40ms single hop for small sequences on our optimized runtime; cross-region adds RTT. For dedicated pools we publish 95th percentile latency in the console per model. We can run a benchmark from your egress points during the pilot 07:30 Priya Nair: pilot — what's a minimal pilot you recommend? 07:35 Marcus Chen: most customers do a 2-week Dedicated trial with a small reserved GPU pool, we help set up VPC peering/privatelink, run a synthetic traffic run and a small eval prompt set for quality + latency. We also support a limited Private on-prem install but that's longer 08:20 Jamal Brooks: fine-grained question — does Redwood's runtime support IP allow-listing for retriever/embedding endpoints? we want to restrict embedding ingestion to certain subnets 08:35 Marcus Chen: yes embedding endpoints can be fronted by private endpoints and we can restrict source CIDRs. For hostnames we issue internal DNS names via privatelink and you can resolve them in your VPC 09:00 Priya Nair: compliance — SOC2 + ISO? we need evidence for procurement 09:06 Lena Ortiz: we are SOC2 type II and have ISO 27001; i'll share the attestation pack. for Private deployments we can provide additional documentation about data flows and network segmentation 10:12 Tom Reynolds: one more — who manages upgrades and patching for Private inside our VPC? we prefer minimal surface area for vendor access 10:23 Marcus Chen: for Private there are two models: 1) Redwood-managed control plane where we only access logs/ops via customer-approved runbooks and scheduled windows; 2) customer-managed control plane where you run the control plane inside your network (we provide the operators and images). Both support limited maintenance windows and RBAC 10:40 Priya Nair: what about SNAT/port translation — we need stable source NAT for outbound webhooks to partners 10:48 Marcus Chen: we can place NAT gateways under your account so egress uses your static IP(s). For Hosted we can allocate dedicated egress IPs to a tenant but Dedicated & Private with your VPC give you full control 12:05 Jamal Brooks: ok we use GCP in some regions — do you support GCP private services connect or just AWS privatelink? 12:14 Marcus Chen: we support both common cloud patterns. On GCP we can use Private Service Connect. Our network guide has cloud-specific sections. We'll send sample manifests for PSC and Privatelink 12:28 Priya Nair: billing & cost questions — if we go Dedicated reserved, can we scale up for short bursts? 12:36 Lena Ortiz: yes Dedicated supports configured autoscaling and burst capacity; pricing is predictable with commitment tiers and overage billing. Redwood Optimize will run suggestions to reduce token cost 13:10 Tom Reynolds: a note on encryption — we need traffic mTLS between our VPC and Redwood services. do you support mTLS for internal endpoints? 13:18 Marcus Chen: yes we support mTLS for private endpoints and we can exchange certs via your PKI or Redwood-managed certs. We'll include recommended cert rotation cadence in the runbook 14:05 Priya Nair: what about the model catalog — if we pin to an open model hosted in eu-west, will any metadata or model weights leave region during background processes? 14:18 Marcus Chen: model weights are resident in the region you select for Dedicated/Private. Background telemetry/metrics are optional and can be routed to your monitoring stack. We'll provide a model residency statement for procurement 15:20 Lena Ortiz: sounds like the three big blockers are: 1) static egress ips 2) region-lock enforcement 3) customer KMS/HSM. we can address all 3 with Private or Dedicated. any other red flags? 15:33 Tom Reynolds: firewall rules: need exact ports for our change board. also, we need to confirm the peering option with our TGW team 15:40 Jamal Brooks: and can you send sample terraform for privatelink + route table entries? 15:48 Marcus Chen: yes we'll provide terraform snippets and a sample CloudFormation if needed. We have a public repo with examples; i'll share link 16:25 Priya Nair: timeline — procurement wants a 6 week runway. is that realistic for Private? 16:33 Lena Ortiz: for Private with our managed control plane it's usually 3-6 weeks depending on approvals and network provisioning. On-prem/on-prem-like is longer. For Dedicated trial we can be faster ~2 weeks to get a proof of latency 16:50 Tom Reynolds: ok can we get a checklist to show legal and compliance?
16:57 Lena Ortiz: yes i'll include SOC2, model residency statement, runbook, and the network checklist. along with sample configs 17:35 Jamal Brooks: any gotchas about multi-region KV cache replication? we don't want cross-border replication without consent 17:43 Marcus Chen: replication is opt-in. default is region-local only. we will never replicate KV cache cross-border unless you enable it. We'll document that setting prominently 18:20 Priya Nair: i'd like to schedule the se deep dive next week to go over our TGW topology and routing policies 18:28 Lena Ortiz: noted — i'll propose times for oct 4th/5th. marcus will own that session 19:05 Tom Reynolds: ok next steps recap? 19:10 Lena Ortiz: sure — lena: send runbook pack, network checklist, terraform samples, SOC2 + model residency. marcus: schedule se session and provide sample terraform and sample egress IP ranges. jamal/priya: confirm preferred pilot window and internal TGW contact 19:30 Priya Nair: works for us, we'll loop in network team and get back by friday with preferred times 19:38 Jamal Brooks: we'll start internal change ticket for peering Action items (recorded in transcript): - Lena: send attestation pack (SOC2/ISO), network checklist, and runbook link (due 2027-09-30) - Marcus: share terraform privatelink + TGW snippets and sample egress ip ranges; propose times for Oct 4th architecture deep dive (due 2027-10-01) - IslandView (Priya/Jamal): confirm pilot window and TGW contact (due 2027-10-01) Links mentioned: - redwood security & runbook (shared link): https://redwood.example.com/security/runbook (placeholder) - terraform examples repo (shared): https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-examples - pilot checklist spreadsheet (note): i will drop in CRM Closing notes: call ends with agreement to run a Dedicated trial with private peering for a short benchmark, and to keep region-locking strict. procurement will need the attestation pack for the 6-week procurement runway. Transcript end.
